mena_gulf.rationale: Facts: Gulf bourses rallied on Nov 4-5 (Dubai +4%, Qatar +2.8%) on bets that the Democratic midterm sweep narrows room for a wider US-Iran war, Aramco beat Q3 estimates, Qatari mediation is active and Iran gives Qatari ships free Hormuz passage. Against that: Brent fell from about $118 to about $99, Aramco cut Asian OSPs $2/bbl, Saudi Q3 oil revenue fell 23% y/y, UKMTO counted at least 11 ships attacked around Hormuz in the week to Nov 6 (3 sank), and the US resumed 'minor strikes' on Qeshm on Nov 6. Interpretation: de-escalation upside and fiscal/kinetic downside offset; explorer rounds split between 0 and -1, so 0 with a downside skew while the FGE strike window (mid-Nov to mid-Dec) is open.

global_equity.rationale: Geopolitical channel only. Facts: the oil war premium unwound (Brent about -13% on the like-for-like Jan contract, Oct 30 to Nov 6), Vance and Trump tied the midterm loss to the war, Qatar says mediation remains active, and the US-China truce is being rolled forward (USTR proposes extending the 301 maritime suspension to Jan 9, 2027; Xi-Trump at APEC Shenzhen Nov 18-19). Against that, Trump confirmed new strikes on Qeshm (Nov 6), Axios/NYT report combat preparations, and FGE sees a high chance of a limited strike before Jan 3. Interpretation: geopolitics is a mild net relief offset by live escalation tail risk, so 0. The Nov 5 AI/semis sell-off (the main -1 driver for global equity in other topics) is a domestic-policy and financing story scored in other pillars and is deliberately not repeated here to avoid double counting.

energy_oil.rationale: Facts: Brent futures settled $117.64 on Oct 30 (expiring Dec contract) and fell to $94.62 on Nov 4 (-8.6%, lowest since Sep 4) before ending near $98-99 on Nov 6; the like-for-like Jan contract fell about 13% on the week (the continuous series overstates the drop by about $4 because of the roll). JPMorgan's surplus widened to 1.4 mb/d, Dubai flipped to contango, Aramco cut December Asian OSPs $2/bbl, and the Nov 29 OPEC+ meeting on 2027 baselines points to a market-share contest; IEA sees a large 2027 surplus once Hormuz reopens. Interpretation: the war premium is deflating and physical signals are loose, so -1; not -2 because attacks continue (11 ships in a week), the US resumed minor strikes and FGE puts a limited-strike window at mid-Nov to mid-Dec, leaving a $10-20 upside gap risk.

regime_notes: The US-Iran war and Hormuz remain the dominant driver for Gulf assets and oil, but US domestic politics now sets the direction: after the Nov 3 Democratic sweep, Vance and Trump tied the loss to the war and Brent lost about 13-15% on the week as markets priced a Qatar-mediated deal. Price is diverging from the physical war: at least 11 ships were attacked around Hormuz in the week to Nov 6 and the US resumed minor strikes on Qeshm, while Iran still demands an end to the blockade, sanctions relief and frozen funds before reopening the strait. Physical oil signals (Dubai contango, JPM 1.4 mb/d surplus, Aramco OSP cut) argue the premium bleeds out slowly absent escalation. The oil-short/importer-long legs (energy_oil, mena_gulf vs india, consumer, govt_bonds) are one paired position that reverses on a single strike decision; FGE puts that window at mid-Nov to mid-Dec. Data hygiene: $118 is the Oct 30 Brent futures settle and $135 the Oct 2 Dated spot print; the Russia-oil tariff waiver is open-ended and revocable at will, not a Dec 15 review.

red_flags.issue: Active regional war: at least 11 ships attacked around Hormuz in the week to Nov 6 (3 sank), IRGC mine claims, Houthi claims on Saudi East-West pipeline pumping stations, drones over Riyadh and Mecca, and Iranian threats to Gulf data centres and cables. Direct physical risk to Gulf holdings and possible market disruption.
